name: Geofence & TRACKi
summary: Automatic attendance when staff cross a geofence, payroll from the result, and a vehicle-tracking product, including a TCP server that reads GPS hardware directly.
oneLiner: GPS workforce tracking and fleet tracking, down to the device protocol.
role: Backend, GPS service and web dashboards

overview.what: An attendance and payroll system for staff who work in the field, and TRACKi, a vehicle-tracking service sold to other businesses. Both run on the same backend and database, separated by role.
overview.who: Managers configure geofences and policies, watch a live map and run payroll. Employees are checked in automatically through a mobile app. TRACKi customers get their own fleet dashboard with devices, geofences, alerts and reports.
overview.problem: Manual check-ins and door-mounted biometrics are slow, easy to game and useless for field staff. A geofence replaces the door with a virtual boundary: cross it, and the attendance record opens or closes by itself.

roleDetail.summary: I built the Django backend, the GPS tracker service and the React dashboards. The Flutter employee app was built together with a teammate.
items: Django backend: 7 apps, 26 models, about 125 REST endpoints and 4 WebSocket consumers
A FastAPI and asyncio TCP service that parses the GT06 and HQ tracker protocols
React dashboards with three role layouts, 43 routes and live Leaflet maps with road snapping
Payroll, suspicious check-in scoring, and TRACKi subscriptions with device quotas
Specifications, deployment runbooks and Arabic client-facing technical documentation

architecture.caption: WebSockets carry location; REST carries everything else.

components.title: Clients
components.body: React dashboards for managers, employees and TRACKi customers; the Flutter employee app streaming GPS; tracker hardware identified by IMEI.

components.title: Django + Channels
components.body: REST for ordinary operations and four WebSocket consumers: employee location in, manager dashboard out, TRACKi live, and a raw device monitor.

components.title: GPS tracker service
components.body: FastAPI and asyncio. Accepts long-lived TCP connections from trackers, validates and decodes packets, and sends commands back down the socket.

components.title: Redis + Celery
components.body: Message broker, channel layer and per-device filter state; a geofence sweep every 30 seconds and an hourly subscription check.

components.title: Mapping services
components.body: Traccar as the production GPS server, OSRM for road snapping, OpenStreetMap tiles and Firebase for push.

implementation.title: Device protocols
implementation.body: GT06, the binary protocol most low-cost trackers speak: start bits 0x78 0x78, length, protocol number, payload, serial number, a CRC-ITU checksum against a 256-entry table, and stop bits 0x0D 0x0A. Plus HQ, an ASCII protocol with NMEA-style coordinates converted to decimal degrees.

implementation.title: TCP server
implementation.body: One asyncio task per connection with a 300-second read timeout so dead sockets are reclaimed. Partial reads are buffered until a whole packet arrives, and packets are decoded into typed dataclasses for login, location, heartbeat and alarm.

implementation.title: Real-time
implementation.body: Django Channels with Redis. The phone streams positions over a WebSocket; crossing a boundary records an entry or exit event and opens or closes the day's attendance.

implementation.title: Database
implementation.body: MySQL, 26 models. A unique constraint on (user, date) means a flaky connection can't create a second attendance record. A one-row-per-employee status table acts as a write-through cache, so the live map is one indexed read.

implementation.title: Payroll
implementation.body: Worked days, late days, absences and overtime calculated from attendance against a configurable policy. Salary profiles are date-ranged and frozen onto each payroll entry.

implementation.title: Mobile
implementation.body: Flutter with BLoC and dependency injection, built with a teammate. An offline queue in Hive replays cached points and check-ins with their original timestamps.

decisions.title: WebSockets for location, REST for everything else
decisions.context: Position data is continuous and latency-sensitive; everything else is ordinary CRUD.
decisions.decision: Split on that line. Location streams over Channels; every other operation is REST.
decisions.tradeoff: Two transports to maintain. Each half stays simple, cacheable and easy to document.

decisions.title: Build our own GPS server, then run Traccar
decisions.context: Parsing tracker packets ourselves removes a dependency; a mature open-source server supports far more hardware.
decisions.decision: Both sit behind one GPS-backend adapter that managers can switch from the dashboard. Traccar is the production path; the custom asyncio server is built and kept switchable.
decisions.tradeoff: Two backends behind one interface, in exchange for a decision that stays reversible. The reasoning is written up in a decision document.

decisions.title: Self-hosted maps after a written cost study
decisions.context: Google Maps, Mapbox and self-hosted OpenStreetMap compared on setup cost, monthly cost at 100, 1,000 and 10,000 devices, lock-in, offline use, and sanctions risk for operating in Syria.
decisions.decision: Self-hosted OpenStreetMap tiles with OSRM for road snapping.
decisions.tradeoff: More to operate ourselves, with no variable cost and no vendor that could switch the service off.

decisions.title: Freeze salary data onto each payslip
decisions.context: A raise next month must not rewrite last month's payslip.
decisions.decision: Each payroll entry stores a JSON snapshot of the salary profile used, and profiles carry effective-from and effective-to dates instead of being overwritten.
decisions.tradeoff: Some duplicated data, in exchange for payroll history that can always be reconstructed.

challenges.problem: A parked vehicle isn't still: consumer GPS drifts about 15 metres between readings, so cars twitched around car parks all night.
challenges.solution: A stationary filter detects stops and locks the displayed position until real movement resumes, with per-device state in Redis so it survives restarts.

challenges.problem: A TCP stream has no request and response pairing, so a device's reply can't be matched to the command that caused it.
challenges.solution: send_command() writes the command and waits on an asyncio Future that the receive loop resolves, guarded by a Lock and a timeout.

challenges.problem: Automatic attendance creates an incentive to fake it.
challenges.solution: Every check-in is scored on distance, reported accuracy, mock-location flags and speed, and marked valid, suspicious or invalid for a manager to review.

challenges.problem: Field staff lose signal, and a dropped check-in is worse than none.
challenges.solution: The app queues points and events offline and replays them through batch endpoints with their original timestamps.

results.status: Private deployment on the client's infrastructure. It needs physical GPS trackers to demonstrate, so there is no public instance; a recorded walkthrough is available on request.

metrics.label: Lines across backend, GPS service and web

notes: Traccar is the live GPS backend. The custom TCP server is built and switchable, not the production path.
The Flutter app was built together with a teammate.
